name: Catecholamine Biosynthesis, Catabolism, and Phaeochromocytoma Diagnostics

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd ed
clinicalPearls: Tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting step in catecholamine synthesis, requiring tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4)
Dopamine beta-hydroxylase requires ascorbic acid (vitamin C); PNMT requires SAM and is induced by cortisol
Catecholamines are degraded by MAO and COMT into metanephrines and vanillylmandelic acid (VMA)
Plasma free metanephrines and 24-hour urine metanephrines provide >97% sensitivity for phaeochromocytoma
Preoperative management of phaeochromocytoma strictly mandates alpha-blockade (phenoxybenzamine) prior to beta-blockade
reference.pathophysiology: Catecholamines are synthesized in chromaffin tissue and central neurons. Phaeochromocytomas hypersecrete norepinephrine and epinephrine autonomously, precipitating paroxysmal alpha-1 mediated arterial vasoconstriction and beta-1 mediated tachycardia. Breakdown by COMT within the tumor produces metanephrines, which enter the circulation. Carcinoid tumors overproduce serotonin from tryptophan, yielding elevated urinary 5-HIAA and endocardial fibrosis.
additionalInvestigations: Fractionated plasma free metanephrines and normetanephrines (fasting, supine draw)
24-Hour urinary fractionated metanephrines, VMA, and creatinine
Adrenal contrast CT / MRI, followed by 123I-MIBG or 68Ga-DOTATATE PET scan
